chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you doubt regarding the life of a sheep, and you see it blink its eye, or move its ears, or beat its tail, then slaughter it, for it is halal (permissible) for you.

key_terms.تَطْرِفُ: blinks/twitches its eye — a sign of life sufficient to permit slaughter
key_terms.تَمْصَعُ بِذَنَبِهَا: beats/wags its tail — an observable sign of life
key_terms.حَلَالٌ: halal — permissible according to Islamic law
key_terms.شَكَكْتَ: you doubt — referring to doubt (shakk) about whether the animal is still alive

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of life in a sheep that make its slaughter permissible according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a jurisprudential ruling on doubtful slaughter: if one doubts whether an animal is still alive before slaughter, visible signs of life — blinking, ear movement, or tail movement — are sufficient indicators that the animal is alive and thus can be validly slaughtered. This ruling addresses a practical concern for those engaged in livestock slaughter, providing clear observable criteria to determine the permissibility of the meat.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Musny Al Hannat, from Aban Bin Taghlub, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘When you doubt regarding the life of a sheep, and you see it blinks its eyes, or moving its ears, or beating its tail, so slaughter it, for it is Permissible for you’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad ibn abu Najran from Muthanna’ al-Hannat from Aban ibn Taghlib who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
in a doubtful condition about a sheep being alive or dead, see if its eyes turn, or its ears move or its tail moves, then slaughter it, it is lawful for food.’”
